source_title: HB-1-3555 SFH Guaranteed Loan Program Technical Handbook
edition: Chapter 9 (Revised 08-05-25 PN 649), Attachment 9-A, Chapter 5 §5.3 (GUS), Chapter 11 §11.2-11.3 (Revised 11-25-25 PN 651)
note: Paraphrased rule records for the USDA Guaranteed (SFHGLP) Golden Loan Path. USDA keeps three distinct income concepts: annual (household) income, adjusted annual income (eligibility) and repayment income (parties to the note). They are never merged into one qualifying-income field. Anchors must exist in the privately cached official slices for the regression step to pass.

rules.text: Annual income includes all eligible income sources from all adult household members, not just parties to the loan note; it is the basis for adjusted annual income, which determines household eligibility.
rules.anchor: all adult household members, not just parties to the loan note

rules.text: Annual income is calculated for the ensuing 12 months from income verifications, documentation and household composition, using gross amounts before payroll deductions of base wages, overtime, commissions, tips, bonuses and other compensation of all adult members; documented cost-of-living or wage increases effective on or before closing are included.
rules.anchor: Annual income is calculated for the ensuing 12 months

rules.text: Include only the first $480 of earned income from adult full-time students who are not an applicant or an applicant's spouse.
rules.anchor: Include the first $480 of earned income from adult full-time students

rules.text: Paystubs/earning statements must contain enough information to calculate income including year-to-date earnings and be dated no earlier than 30 days before the initial loan application date; W-2s must cover the most recent one or two years as applicable.
rules.anchor: dated no earlier than 30 days prior to the initial loan application date

rules.text: A verbal verification of employment (or written/e-mail confirmation other than a paystub) must be obtained for all applicants within 10 business days of loan closing, naming the person who completed it for the employer.
rules.anchor: within 10 business days of loan closing

rules.text: Alternative income documentation: a written VOE (electronic employer verification, Form RD 1910-5 or an equivalent HUD/VA/Fannie/Freddie form) verifying current YTD and previous-year earnings, plus a recent paycheck/earnings statement.
rules.anchor: Form RD 1910-5, Request for Verification of Employment

rules.text: Adjusted annual income is the annual income minus the eligible deductions in 7 CFR 3555.152(c) (dependents, child care, elderly household, care of household members with disabilities, medical expenses); it determines program eligibility.
rules.anchor: subtracting any of the eligible deductions in 7 CFR 3555.152(c)

rules.text: Repayment income is the stable and dependable income of the applicants who will be parties to the note; its calculation often differs from annual and adjusted annual income. Co-signers and non-occupant co-borrowers are not permitted.
rules.anchor: stable and dependable income of the applicants who will be parties to the note

rules.text: Repayment income sources must be documented with evidence of historical receipt and a likelihood of continuance for at least three years; gaps in employment are analyzed by the lender (the Agency sets no specific gap criteria).
rules.anchor: continuance for at least 3 years into the mortgage

rules.text: A sharp increase or a documented decrease in earnings is a 20 percent or greater variance from the previous 12 months; the lender must determine whether an increase is supported and logical, or whether a decrease continues or has stabilized.
rules.anchor: 20 percent or greater variance in income from the previous 12 months

rules.text: Base wages (hourly or salary, full or part time): required history one year, which may be met through a combination of employers, education or military service; income must be received at the time of submission.
rules.anchor: The one year of required history may be met through a combination of employers, education, or military service

rules.text: Base wages documentation options: paystub(s)/earning statement(s), W-2s, written or electronic VOE, or federal income tax returns/IRS transcripts with all schedules.
rules.anchor: Written Verification of Employment (VOE) or electronic verifications

rules.text: Depository accounts (checking, money market, savings): two months of recent bank statements, or a VOD plus a recent official monthly statement, or TPV verification covering at least the most recent 60 days (data current within 30 days).
rules.anchor: Two months of recent bank statements

rules.text: Investigate all recurring deposits not attributed to wages (no tolerance) to rule out undisclosed income, and investigate individual non-recurring deposits greater than $1,000.
rules.anchor: Investigate individual (non-recurring) deposits greater than $1,000

rules.text: GUS provides a credit evaluation and underwriting recommendation; it concludes credit and capacity are acceptable or refers the loan to the lender's underwriter for manual underwriting. Applicants must not be approved or denied solely on a GUS risk assessment, and GUS does not evaluate the dependability of repayment income.
rules.anchor: should not be approved or denied a SFHGLP guarantee solely on the basis of a risk assessment generated by GUS

rules.text: GUS checks that the property is in an eligible rural area and that adjusted annual household income meets the adjusted income limits for the household size, county and state.
rules.anchor: adjusted annual household income meets the adjusted income limits

rules.text: Final GUS data must match the loan file or fall within Agency tolerances; an increase in obligations must not exceed a cumulative total of $50.
rules.anchor: do not exceed a cumulative total of $50

rules.text: Ratios use repayment income; applicants have repayment ability when the proposed monthly housing expense (PITI) does not exceed 29 percent of repayment income.
rules.anchor: does not exceed 29 percent of their repayment income

rules.text: Applicants have repayment ability when total debts (PITI plus other monthly obligations) do not exceed 41 percent of repayment income.
rules.anchor: do not exceed 41 percent of their repayment income

rules.text: All open debts incurred through the closing date must be considered and documented in GUS and the application; credit report amounts are used unless verification supports an alternate payment.
rules.anchor: Amounts listed on the credit report will be used unless verification supports an alternate payment amount
